catalysts.watch: Chip export growth vs +46.7% in the first ten days
catalysts.plain: South Korea's chip exports are the earliest hard data on chip demand. A sharp slowdown would be an early warning.

catalysts.watch: Hike or hold; guidance on December
catalysts.plain: The Fed decides on interest rates. Another rise, or hints of one, makes borrowing for AI more expensive.

catalysts.event: Q3 results: Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon (expected 27-30 Oct)
catalysts.watch: 2026 capex vs guidance, first 2027 capex color, cloud growth, AI revenue, financing plans
catalysts.plain: The biggest test of the month. If any of them cuts AI spending plans, that is historically the clearest sign a boom is ending.
Full-month chip export numbers from South Korea.
The election could change taxes, spending and trade policy.
TSMC makes most AI chips; its monthly sales show whether demand is holding.

catalysts.event: US October CPI; BofA November survey; CoreWeave Q3 results (to be confirmed)
catalysts.watch: Inflation path; fund-manager cash and crowded trade; neocloud liquidity and backlog
catalysts.plain: Inflation decides the Fed's next step, the survey shows how crowded investors are, and CoreWeave's results show how the most indebted AI company is coping.

catalysts.event: Nvidia Q3 FY27 results (after close) and FOMC minutes
catalysts.watch: Revenue vs the $108B guide, FY28 outlook, DSO, guarantees, and the share-price reaction
catalysts.plain: Nvidia is the bellwether of the AI boom. Watch the share price the next day: falling even on great results means good news is already priced in.

catalysts.watch: Pricing vs the $965B private round and $1.5-2T talk; first-month trading
catalysts.plain: If the listing is delayed, priced low, or trades below its first price, money for AI is drying up.

catalysts.watch: ~77% odds of a hike priced as of 19 Oct; the dot plot
catalysts.plain: Another Fed decision on interest rates, with its forecast for next year.

catalysts.event: Oracle, Broadcom and Micron results (to be confirmed)
catalysts.watch: Oracle capex and financing; Broadcom customer backstops; memory pricing
catalysts.plain: Oracle is the biggest borrower in the AI build-out; Micron shows where memory prices are heading.

catalysts.watch: The same funding-window tests as Anthropic
catalysts.plain: Another test of whether investors will keep paying high prices for AI companies.
